alignments.note: The one expressed verb serves both subjects; the ASV gaps it and supplies 'so doth' for the second clause, which rides with the answering conjunction rather than echoing back onto this verb (see s007).
Substantival article before a prepositional phrase keeps the discontinuous pronoun and relativizer under rule 32; no participle follows to carry the relativizer.
The supplied copula rides with the prepositional predicate under rules 32 and 53.
One adjective glossed by the whole phrase; the syn- prefix's complement 'together with you' is a rule 7 helper, and rule 17 heads on the meaning-bearing 'elect'.

The supplied verb of a gapped clause rides with the answering conjunction that introduces it, as 2PE.3.16's kai -> '*they do* also' and REV.6.11's 'even as they were' do; rule 88's principle that an obligatory English juncture is a helper on what it introduces points the same way, and rule 86 is not reached because an expressed conjunction licenses the supplied words. The conjunction keeps its own 'and' as head under rule 17. Medium as at 2PE.3.16, the alternative being to echo 'so doth' back onto aspazetai across the whole subject phrase.
Displaced by the possessive on the genitive pronoun under rule 20.
